newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds likely bidder for Abbey - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds likely bidder for Abbey - analysts.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group Plc is a more likely bidder for life insurer Lloyds Abbey Life Plc than giant insurer Prudential Corp Plc, cited as a bidder in the market on Wednesday, insurance analysts said.
Shares in Lloyds Abbey Life rocketed on the take-over speculation, peaking at 607 pence before falling back slightly to 595 pence, up 34.5 pence.

Lloyds TSB already holds a 62 percent stake in the life insurer and after the merger between Lloyds and TSB last December, Lloyds Abbey Life has said it is discussing a range of options which may mean restructuring.

Insurance analysts said the life insurer was considering a range of strategic options, ranging from doing nothing to closing down altogether, under a steering group run by its chief executive Stephen Maran.
Maran, and other officials at Lloyds Abbey Life, were not immediately available for comment.
But, at the time of Lloyds Abbey Life's interim results in July, finance director Laurel Powers-Freeling told Reuters the talks had not been concluded.
"There is a range of options, there are a number of permutations," Powers-Freeling said then.
"We're waiting for an announcement," one analyst said.
ABN Amro Hoare Govett analyst John Russell said he thought Lloyds Abbey Life was an unlikely bid target for Prudential.
"Prudential is more likely to demutualise a mutual and get access to IFAs," said Russell.
"I give very little credence to a bid by the Pru," he said.
More likely is that Lloyds will pick up the remaining stake or do a deal with the minority holders to give back Abbey Life and personal loans finance arm Bowmaker.
"They may unravel it...and give Abbey Life back to the minority shareholders," said Russell.
Analysts said that among the minority holders of Lloyds Abbey Life was PDFM Limited, the fund management arm of UBS.
"It's more likely that Lloyds it going to try and buy out the minority," said the unnamed analyst.
When it merged with TSB last year Lloyds acquired a life assurance operation and analysts said one possibilty was to merge the two insurance operations.
Analysts also pointed to comments by Lloyds TSB chief executive Sir Brian Pitman in June when he said the bank had no plans to increase its stake in the insurer.
They said Lloyds Abbey Life was a good business, noting its pre-tax profits in the first half were up 28 percent at 259.2 million stg.

The analyst said that, with the increase in profit, he had increased the valuation of Lloyds Abbey Life's shares to around 600 pence, closer to the level at which the shares were trading on Wednesday. Russell said he had done the same.

Lloyds TSB and Prudential both said they did not comment on market rumours. Dealers said Prudential was cited as a bidder after it receieved 1.75 billion stg from the sale of Mercantile and General reinsurance to Swiss Re on Tuesday.
